title: Signed Kuramoto networks inside positive ones: an exact realisation theorem, stable non-manifold equilibria, and Sclosa's closed-manifold conjecture
shortTitle: Signed Kuramoto networks inside positive ones
oneLine: Every ±1 signed Kuramoto network sits exactly inside a network with only positive couplings, with equilibria and stability preserved; this yields a 324-oscillator attractive network whose stable equilibria form a cone over a torus, refuting the closed-manifold and immersed readings of Sclosa's Conjecture 1.3, while its literal arXiv v1 reading is true.
abstract: Networks of identical phase oscillators with attractive (positive) coupling are the simplest models of synchronisation. This candidate proves that every ±1 signed Kuramoto network is reproduced exactly on an invariant torus of a positive unweighted network: replace each oscillator by a ring of six groups of r clones at phase offsets aπ/3, and realise a negative edge as a matching between groups whose offsets differ by π. For r > 4Δ the complete set of nearby equilibria, the Morse index, the nullity and Lyapunov stability all transfer, because a uniform normal Hessian bound gives an energy inequality even at degenerate equilibria. Applications: a connected 23-regular graph on 324 vertices whose equilibrium set near one stable point is ℝ × C(S¹ × S¹), a cone over a torus, with every nearby equilibrium stable; stable cones ℝ × C(S^k × S^k) for every k ≥ 1; stable crossing tori on 120 vertices; stable smooth continua of every dimension. For Sclosa's Conjecture 1.3, the readings refuted are the published one (a finite union of closed manifolds), its countable version, the version with immersed compact pieces, and pieces closed only relative to the equilibrium or stable set; neither the equilibrium set nor the stable set admits such a cover. The literal arXiv v1 reading (a finite union of manifolds, not necessarily closed) is true for every graph by stratification, as is the reading with boundary allowed. On K_n a closed or immersed compact cover exists exactly when n is odd or n ≤ 4. Everything occurs at exact symmetric resonances and is not robust to generic perturbation.

evidence: Written proofs of every result in an 18-page manuscript: the exact signed-to-positive realisation theorem with a uniform normal Hessian bound and normal-coercivity energy inequality, the local cone in angle coordinates, closed- and immersed-cover obstructions, the complete-graph classification and three further applications. An exact integer eigenbasis certificate of the Jacobian at the cone point of G_{6,r} for r = 9, 8, 7; floating-point checks on ten random signed graphs (296 equilibria), repulsive complete-graph lifts and a weighted variant; nine semantic negative controls; replay from a clean copy and from the frozen archive, and in GitHub CI.
statusDetail: Unrefereed AI-assisted mathematical candidate. Every result has a written proof; key spectra are certified in exact integer arithmetic. Internal AI-assisted review in five roles, two automated correctness reviews, a targeted proof audit, a verification re-review and a fresh-context check of the final corrections only. External specialist review, independent reproduction and formal verification have not been established. Scope: exact symmetric resonances.

Related works are taken verbatim from the manuscript bibliography; every DOI was resolved at doi.org and its title matched on Crossref on 27 October 2026.
keyResults: Realisation (Theorem 1): every ±1 signed simple graph with maximum degree Δ is reproduced exactly on an invariant torus of a positive unweighted graph G(H,r), r > 4Δ, with 6nr vertices; complete equilibrium germs, Lyapunov stability, Morse index and nullity transfer.

Stable cone (Theorem 2): G_{6,9}, 324 vertices and 3726 edges, 23-regular, has an equilibrium whose equilibrium germ is ℝ × C(S¹ × S¹), with every nearby equilibrium Lyapunov stable; the Jacobian there has 5 zero and 319 negative eigenvalues (exact certificate).

Sclosa's Conjecture 1.3: refuted in its published closed-manifold wording, its countable version, its immersed-compact version and its relatively-closed version, for both the equilibrium set and the stable set; true in its literal arXiv v1 wording (manifolds not necessarily closed) and with boundary allowed.
Classification (Theorem 3): on K_n a closed (or immersed compact) manifold cover exists exactly when n is odd or n ≤ 4.

Applications: stable cones ℝ × C(S^k × S^k) for every k ≥ 1 (Corollary 13), stable crossing tori on 120 vertices (Corollary 14), stable smooth continua of every dimension (Corollary 15); r = 9 is sufficient, r ≤ 7 is unstable and r = 8 is open (Remark 12).

narration: Signed Kuramoto networks inside positive ones. An Evidence Press briefing. First, the background. Picture a network of identical oscillators, such as metronomes on a shared table, each nudging its neighbours. Usually every link pulls neighbours into step. A resting state is an arrangement where all the nudges cancel, and it is stable if small disturbances stay small. In twenty twenty-three, Davide Sclosa conjectured that these resting states always form a finite union of closed manifolds: a few tidy, smooth, closed pieces. Now, the main findings. First, links that push oscillators apart can be built exactly from links that pull. Each oscillator is replaced by a ring of copies, offset by sixty degrees, and a pushing link joins copies that are half a turn apart, where a pull acts exactly like a push. Everything near every resting state, including stability, carries over unchanged. Second, using this, a network of three hundred and twenty-four oscillators with only pulling links has a whole family of stable resting states that, at one point, is shaped like a cone over a torus, not a smooth surface. So the conjecture fails as published, with closed pieces, and also if the pieces may cross themselves. But its first arXiv version said only a finite union of manifolds, without the word closed, and that version is true, by a standard theorem on algebraic sets. Why it matters: singular families of stable states are possible even when every link is attractive. The limitations: everything happens at an exact, symmetric balance, and generic small changes destroy it. This is an unrefereed, AI-assisted candidate, released on twenty-seven October twenty twenty-six. The paper, proofs and checks are linked on this page. This briefing uses a synthetic AI voice, and is not additional evidence.

Syst. 22(4), 2023) for homogeneous Kuramoto equilibria: refuted in its closed-manifold, countable, immersed-compact and relatively-closed readings, for the equilibrium set and the stable set; true in its literal arXiv v1 reading and with boundary allowed.
decisionObject.scope: Homogeneous Kuramoto flow with unit couplings on finite simple graphs; counterexamples at exact symmetric resonances (K_6 and its positive lift G_{6,9}).
